Echo shows marked left atrial enlargement (52 mm) with normal LV wall thickness and mild pulmonary hypertension, suggesting chronic diastolic dysfunction/HFpEF and atrial remodeling rather than primary LV systolic cardiomyopathy. The initial ECG shows sinus bradycardia with markedly prolonged P-wave duration (180 ms) and biphasic P waves in II/III/aVF — findings characteristic of advanced interatrial block (Bayés syndrome), which strongly predisposes to atrial tachyarrhythmias. There is first-degree AV block (PR 280 ms) and a widened QRS with an rsR' in V1 consistent with intraventricular conduction delay / incomplete RBBB pattern, indicating conduction system disease. The follow-up ECG demonstrates atrial flutter, which fits the palpitations and the atrial enlargement / interatrial block. Severe hypertension (BP 221/85) may have precipitated decompensation and contributes to chronic atrial remodeling. Taken together the most likely primary problems are an atrial tachyarrhythmia (atrial flutter) on a background of atrial cardiomyopathy/interatrial block and HFpEF; sinus-node and AV conduction disease and hypertensive crisis are important contributors/alternatives.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Atrial flutter (atrial macro‑reentrant tachyarrhythmia) on background of left atrial enlargement — suggested by follow‑up ECG showing flutter and by palpitations/atrial remodeling.
2. Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)/diastolic heart failure — elevated BNP, dyspnea, LA enlargement, normal LV wall thickness.
3. Advanced interatrial block (Bayés syndrome) / atrial conduction abnormality — prolonged P wave (180 ms) with biphasic inferior leads, explaining predisposition to atrial flutter/fibrillation.
4. Sinus node dysfunction / tachy‑brady syndrome (sick sinus spectrum) — baseline sinus bradycardia with episodic atrial tachyarrhythmia.
5. Hypertensive emergency / severe uncontrolled hypertension with acute decompensation — BP 221/85 contributing to chest tightness, dyspnea and heart failure exacerbation.
